$comment: Colour themes for the Azkript brand mark.
Each theme is a complete set of stops for the one document glyph, so the
composition stays identical and only the light changes. scripts/brand-lab.cjs
renders every theme side by side at true pixel sizes for comparison;
scripts/build-brand.cjs bakes `selected` into app/brand/azkript-mark*.svg.
Sheet ramp: four stops from the lit upper-left to the deep lower-right. Keep
the LIGHT end clearly desaturated and the DARK end clearly saturated-deep: that
is what gives the Fluent glyph its volume without an outline. Avoid a flat
three-stop ramp, which reads as a plain fill at 32 px.
Badge ramp: three stops of a DEEPER shade of the same hue, not neutral black.
The badge must read as a separate plane on the sheet, and a same-hue darker
plane does that; a neutral badge reads as a hole punched through the glyph.
Badge ramps are DERIVED by scripts/derive-badge-ramps.py against the measured
2025 Office conventions (badge lightness 0.39-0.71, badge-vs-sheet contrast
1.6-3.6, same hue family) and CHECKED by scripts/palette-audit.cjs. A theme may
set `badgeLocked: true` to keep a badge that was chosen by eye instead, which is
necessary for warm hues: darkening amber desaturates it toward brown at every
saturation value, so the vivid answer is a hue-shifted terracotta and that is a
judgement call, not a search result. Locked badges are still audited.
Fold/rule/shadow colours are per-theme because a warm sheet needs a warm
shadow and a white rule needs to stay clean against a pale light stop.
Saturation of the sheet's light stop matters more than it looks: the heading
rule sits near the bright corner, so a light stop that is too pale makes the
white content lines vanish. palette-audit.cjs enforces the contrast floor.

amber.label: Amber / copper
amber.rationale: Warm paper under a desk lamp: the one warm hue in the productivity space that no Office-family app claims. Reads as a script page rather than as a spreadsheet or a slide.
amber.badgeNote: Chosen by eye in scripts/badge-lab.cjs. The numeric search keeps producing a browner badge because darkening amber desaturates it; this red-shifted terracotta stays vivid against the sheet, which is the same trick PowerPoint uses (orange sheet, red badge).

garnet.label: Garnet / crimson
garnet.rationale: The colour of a marked-up script and of PowerPoint's warm end, but deeper and redder so it does not read as PowerPoint orange.

rose.label: Rose / magenta
rose.rationale: Vivid and unclaimed; the closest neighbour is OneNote's purple, which is a different family (violet, not pink).

violet.label: Violet / indigo
violet.rationale: OneNote owns purple in the Office family, and Figma owns multicolour, so this is the most contested candidate of the set.

teal.label: Teal / cyan
teal.rationale: Clean and technical; Teams sits nearby but at a greener, flatter hue, and cyan is otherwise unclaimed by document apps.

forest.label: Forest / green
forest.rationale: Excel owns green in the Office family; included for comparison so the reader can see the collision.

graphite.label: Graphite / slate
graphite.rationale: Neutral, and the safest choice if the icon must not compete with any other app on the taskbar; the cost is that a neutral sheet carries less of the Fluent 'saturated body' character.
